claim: A bounded, leakage-controlled open-data workflow learns a self-supervised CTG representation for interpretable neonatal-risk enrichment and calibration, with external CTG datasets used for representation transfer only.
SSL representations are evaluated as an exploratory risk-enrichment and interpretation layer alongside classical signal features.
Route-independent signal phenotypes link adverse clinical profile, expert CTG morphology and perturbation-stable same-cohort mechanism directions.
Cross-fitted Platt recalibration improves absolute risk calibration and threshold behavior.
Transformer configuration, masking, objective loss, and feature-family sensitivity support the AI method layer.
CTGDL-FHRMA supports external representation projection and domain-shift assessment, not external neonatal-outcome validation.
Endpoint-threshold and dimensionality checks support sensitivity-bound interpretation under sparse severe-event counts.
